overview.description: Kasino (Swedish Casino) is a classic fishing game played in Sweden. It uses Royal capture values (J=11, Q=12, K=13; Ace 1 or 14). Players capture table cards by matching rank or by a set that sums to the played card's value; captures are optional. First to 16 points wins. The 10 of Diamonds (Storan) and 2 of Spades (Lillan) score extra; sweeps (tabbe) and last capture (sistan) also score.

history.origins: Part of the larger North European 'Nordic Casino' group, it was brought to Sweden in the 19th century. It diverged from traditional English and Russian Casino through the inclusion of 'Royal' face card values (J=11, Q=12, K=13).
timeline: 1880s: First documented in Swedish gaming manuals.
1920s: The 'Storan/Lillan' terminology becomes universal in Swedish households.
Present: Popular family game, known for being easy to learn but difficult to master due to the 16-point 'In-Hand' rule.
history.evolution: The Swedish variant retained a slightly more balanced scoring system than the Finnish version, with Spades being less dominant over other categories.
history.cultural: In Sweden, clearing the table is called a tabbe (or tabellå), worth one extra point, similar to Finnish mökki.

setup.dealing: Deal 4 cards to each player and 4 face-up to the table. This is repeated until the deck is empty.

rules.objective: Capture scoring cards to reach 16 cumulative points.
rules.gameplay: Each turn play one card from hand. Capture a table card of the same capture value, or a set of table cards whose values sum to your card's value; you may take multiple such captures with one play. Capture is optional. Ace counts as 1 or 14. Clearing the table (tabbe) scores 1; last player to capture gets remaining table cards and 1 point (sistan).
keyRules: Capture by same value or by a set of table cards summing to the played card's value; multiple captures allowed in one turn.
Capture is never compulsory; you may leave capturable cards or trail without capturing.
First to 16 or more points wins; tie-break by most points then most spades.
Tabbe (sweep): clearing the table scores 1; sistan: last capture gets remaining table cards and 1 point.

strategy.basic: Keep track of the number of cards you've captured. The 'Most Cards' bonus is often the tie-breaker in close games.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Lillan' Trap: Because the 2 of Spades is worth 15 in hand, players often 'build' a 15 on the table using an Ace and a King, then wait to capture it with the Lillan for a point.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Stalling: If you suspect your opponent has the Storan (10D), avoid leaving a combination of cards on the table that sums to 16 (e.g., 9 and 7).
tips: Don't waste an Ace for a single capture unless it secures the round (last trick). Save it to sweep multiple small cards worth Spades.
The last person to take a card from the table at the end of the deck takes all the remaining 'trash' cards.

edgeCases.text: Tabbe: clearing the table scores 1 point; capturing card is placed face up in pile.
Sistan: when the last cards are played, remaining table cards go to the last player who made a capture; that player scores 1 point. Last card that sweeps scores 2 (sistan plus tabbe).
Ties for most spades or most cards: those points are not awarded.
Ace has capture value 1 or 14 at player's choice when played from hand.

synthesis.shortDescription: Kasino (Swedish Casino) is a classic fishing game played in Sweden. While sharing the 'Royal' capture values of its Finnish counterpart, the Swedish version features distinct scoring (1 point for most spades instead of 2) and emphasizes a 16-point winning match. It is a game of strategic capture where the 10 of Diamonds ('Storan') and the 2 of Spades ('Lillan') are the primary targets.
